summary: _(d) Pending hearing and final disposal of the Petition, pass an ad-interim Order directing the Respondents, jointly and severally to pay 75% of the amounts due to the Petitioner of the amount claimed above."_ 11. The matter was again listed for the hearing on 3.7.2025, wherein the Petitioner apprised the Commission that the Appeal No.168 of 2020, filed by the Respondent, PTCIL, has been dismissed by the APTEL in its judgment dated 8.5.2025. The Respondents are, however, yet to make any payment in terms of the Commission’s order dated 15.8.2020. The Petitioner sought liberty to file an affidavit to place on record the updated details of its claims in terms of the said order. Considering that, the Commission adjourned the matter and permitted the Petitioner to file its additional affidavit and also directed the parties to file their brief notes. (v) It is pertinent to note that in the original Petition filed by the Petitioner (Petition No. 158/MP/2020) wherein the Petitioner agitated its claim for unpaid capacity charges under Article 8.5 of the PPA, PTC and TANGEDCO both admitted the claim of the Petitioner in clear, categorical, and unambiguous (vi) In the present execution proceedings, PTC is seeking to raise disputes on the merits of the claim made by the Petitioner, and that too, after having admitted the said claim in the original proceeding culminating in the order. The purported objections raised by the Respondents with regard to availability of Plant to dispute the Petitioner’s claim, firstly amounts to going behind the order dated 15.8.2020 passed by the Commission (which is impermissible in law in execution proceedings), secondly, the said objections are in face of clear and unequivocal admission of the Petitioner’s claim and Respondents’ corresponding liability, made by Respondents before the Commission and recorded in the order dated 15.8.2020. (i) As per Article 8.5 of the PPA, it is evident that in case of failure to make payment, the Petitioner was initially entitled to sell 25% of the contracted power to a third party, and in case of further delay in payment, the Petitioner was entitled to sell 100% of the capacity to a third party. Further, the amount received by the Petitioner from the sale to a third party was to be adjusted against the liability of PTC/TANGEDCO. Further, the Petitioner has not demonstrated how much of the power was sold to a third party. (viii) The above information and subsequent objection raised by Respondent No.1 are crucial to adjudicate the dispute, and these objections are to be taken into consideration while passing any order in the instant execution petition. (iii) During the entire period of pendency of the present Petition, PTC did not raise any invoices against TANGEDCO, calling upon it to pay the amount which is the subject matter of the dispute in this present Petition. In fact, PTC, by way of its affidavit dated 16.5.2023, has given details of the discrepancies between the invoices that the Petitioner has raised upon PTC, and the invoices which PTC has raised upon TANGEDCO in turn. It is PTC’s specific stand that it did not raise invoices under the _bona fide_ belief that as (sic) the order of the Commission was challenged before the APTEL”. The above conduct of PTC is also noted by the APTEL in its judgment dated 8.5.2025. _Issue No. 1: In terms of PTC-PPA and Procurer-PPA, whose obligation is it for payment towards supply of power by the Petitioner?_ _82. The Appellant’s main argument is that the CERC after recognizing that the Procurer-PPA and PTC-PPA were back-to-back agreements, still held the Appellant liable to pay Respondent No.2._ _86. Appellant contended that under the back-to-back agreement, the Appellant was only acting like a conduit/ intermediary in the whole transaction, placing reliance on the following cases decided by this Tribunal:_ 19. The issue being agitated in the present execution Petition revolves around the objections which were already addressed by the Commission in the impugned order, the findings of which were also affirmed by the APTEL in Appeal No. 168/2020. The issue with respect to the role of PTC being a trader has already been settled. Both the PPAs, i.e. PTC-APNRL and PTC-TANGEDCO, are back-to-back and interlinked in nature. The payment liability of PTC to APNRL is not conditional upon receiving the 20. Regarding another contention of PTC that the Commission has ignored whether the Petitioner sold power to third parties and if such earnings should be set off, it is noted that PTC neither raised such objections during the proceedings before the Commission. Furthermore, the same averments were also rejected by the APTEL, as they were not pleaded before the Commission in the original proceedings. 21. Moreover, in the present execution Petition, the Respondents, PTC and TANGEDCO, have raised contention that the Petitioner is not liable for the claim of capacity charges as in Unit-II of the Petitioner, there was a forced outage between 6.12.2018 to 7.2.2019, and also there was a forced outage in Unit-II of the Petitioner’s plant between 14.1.2019 to 21.1.2019. Further, they have sought to raise disputes on the merits of the claim made by the Petitioner, and that too, after having admitted the said claim in the original proceeding culminating in the order. It is relevant to note here that during the proceedings before the Commission, PTC and TANGEDCO have admitted the claims of the Petitioner for the unpaid capacity charges under Article 8.5 of the PPA, which was allowed by the Commission in the order dated 15.8.2020. At the present stage of the execution proceedings, the Respondents cannot be permitted to raise this issue, belatedly, wherein the scope of the Petition is limited, considering the fact that the APTEL has already dismissed the appeal filed by PTC.
